description: One worker whose badge was scanned into the buckets that went into this bin. The accountability chain from a pack line back to a person: a bin tag is what a packing house holds, and this is the only row that says whose fruit is inside it.

fields.description: The worker. A Link rather than a badge string, because a badge is reassigned between seasons and a settlement question asked two years later is about the person.
fields.label: Employee

fields.description: Denormalised at write time, so a bin read years later names the person as they were named then — the same rule every other record in this app snapshots a name under.
fields.label: Employee Name

fields.description: The badge that was actually scanned, as it was scanned. Kept beside the Employee rather than instead of it: the badge is what the checker's phone saw and the link is what it resolved to, and a dispute about a mis-scan needs both.
fields.label: Badge Scanned

fields.description: How many of this bin's buckets came from this person, where the checker's phone counted per badge. ZERO IS A REAL ANSWER and is not the same as absent: a worker whose badge was scanned at the bin and whose buckets were not separately counted is a contributor with an unknown share, which is honest, and a share invented by dividing the bin evenly would be a piece-rate figure nobody measured.
fields.label: Buckets Contributed

fields.description: The first badge scan counted into this bin, where the phone reported one.
fields.label: First Scan

fields.description: The last badge scan counted into this bin. Together with the first, it is the window this person was tipping into it — which is what a re-entry-interval or a heat-exposure question about a named bin is actually asking.
fields.label: Last Scan

name: Bin Seal Contributor
